# Opal Pettigrew

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043)</sub>

## Appearance

Opal is a dark-eyed girl known for her striking, highly attractive beauty. She has a fair complexion.

_Sources: [v1 c28 P3](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0003), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043)_

## Personality

Opal is overly obsessed with romance, attention, and boys. She loves having admirers and hearing compliments, and she is easily overwhelmed by romantic gestures until she spots insincerity. She can be squeamish or timid during dramatic situations, such as pretending to lie still as if deceased.

_Sources: [v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001), [v2 c26 P56](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0056), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059)_

## Traits

- strikingly attractive  <sub>[v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043)</sub>
- fond of romance and suitors  <sub>[v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v2 c26 P56](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0056), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059)</sub>
- easily frightened or uncomfortable playing dead  <sub>[v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001)</sub>

## Abilities

- curing warts using an enchanted stone

## Goals

- to possess dozens of beaus  <sub>[v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059)</sub>

## History

Opal grew up in a household with multiple older sisters, which gave her early exposure to courtship and suitors. During her school years, she attended school and Regent's with Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke. On one midsummer afternoon, she joined Isolde, Odette Pullen, and Nell at the pond near Pear Hill to act out Tennyson's poem of Elaine, taking on the role of King Arthur because she was too afraid to lay still in the dory to play Elaine. Over time, she acquired an enchanted stone from Old Mary Joe of the Creek to cure her warts. Later, while living in Delford, Nelson Atkins proposed to her in a romantic manner. Opal requested a week to think it over, but upon discovering that his entire proposal was lifted verbatim from a book titled 'The Complete Guide to Etiquette,' she wrote him a blistering rejection.

_Sources: [v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001), [v1 c28 P7](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0007), [v1 c28 P11](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0011), [v2 c26 P56](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0056), [v2 c26 P58](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0058)_
